requirement:
The authoring harness MUST use Rig and support Bedrock, Ollama, and OpenAI. Users MUST be
able to select a backend and model through configuration without changing the
assessment tools, prompt, or evidence format.
rationale:
structural: The text has two structural obligations. (1) "MUST use Rig": an implementation on a hand-written HTTP client or another LLM library would behave the same but would violate this clause. (2) "support Bedrock, Ollama, and OpenAI" with backend and model chosen by configuration: a build with only one backend, or with backends hard-coded instead of chosen from configuration, would violate it. Keeping assessment tools, prompt and evidence format unchanged is observable behavior. It is not a structural obligation.

`crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/providers.rs#impl[RigProvider]/fn[connect]` matches on `BackendConfig`. It builds a Rig completion model for each of Bedrock (`rig_bedrock`), OpenAI (`rig_core` openai responses) and Ollama (`rig_core` ollama native completion). Each model is type-erased into one `model` field, so the backend and model name come only from configuration. Nothing downstream depends on which backend was chosen, apart from provider-specific options.

`crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/providers.rs#impl[RigProvider/CompletionProvider]/fn[complete]` sends every request through the same Rig model with `self.model.call(request)`. That is the common interface the tools, prompt and evidence format sit on top of.

The configuration enum (`src/config.rs#enum[BackendConfig]`) and its mapping to Rig are covered by the refining requirements `requirements.authoring.configuration_storage` and `requirements.authoring.rig_configuration_mapping`. The enum is also reached through the marked `connect`. No further root is needed.

behavioral: The text has one structural obligation (use Rig), which needs no behavioral test here. It has two behavioral obligations.

1. Support Bedrock, Ollama and OpenAI, with the backend and model chosen by configuration.
   - `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[all_adapters_preserve_prompt_tools_and_evidence_with_default_connections]` drives the CLI against a mock server for each backend. Each run is selected by its config file.
     - Ollama: the request body `model` equals `MODEL`, and no authorization header is sent.
     - Bedrock: the request path is `/model/default-chain-model/converse`, and the SDK default chain supplies credentials and region.
     - OpenAI: the request goes to `/responses` with a Bearer key, and the body `model` is `fixture-openai`.
   - `fn[bedrock_cli_uses_selected_profile_region_and_converse_tools]` covers Bedrock model selection, the profile and the region, in both typed and untyped tool-call forms. It checks native history replay and the usage backend and model.
   - `fn[openai_responses_replays_tool_calls_and_records_usage]` covers OpenAI selection, the model, and the request history across tool calls.
   - `fn[authoring_uses_nearest_workspace_configuration_without_a_user_file]` covers Ollama selected through a workspace configuration, with the model checked in the request and in usage.
   - `mod[tests]/fn[typed_client_calls_preserve_order_and_native_history]` and `fn[malformed_typed_client_calls_are_reported]` in `providers.rs` cover Bedrock tool-call normalization.
   - `tests/live_bedrock.rs#fn[live_bedrock_authoring]` is a live check.

2. Changing the backend or model must not change the assessment tools, prompt or evidence format.
   - The all-adapters test runs identical projects and submissions through the three backends. It asserts that `prompt_and_tools` is equal across Ollama, Bedrock and OpenAI. That helper compares the prompt text and the sorted tool names, descriptions and schemas, with only the provider envelopes stripped.
   - It asserts there are 12 tools.
   - It asserts the entire evidence JSON is equal across all three backends.
   - The Bedrock and OpenAI tests also check the tool set, the tool schemas and the prompt content.

The tests both exercise these behaviors and assert their outcomes, so I found no unaddressed gap.
